title: Fenofibrate in WWOX-LoF
summary: An experimental comparison of systemic fuel handling and direct neural action.

graph.evidence: Global Wwox loss can lower circulating glucose.
graph.inference: Neuronal rescue can also normalize systemic glucose.
graph.hypothesis: Systemic fuel support or direct neural signaling could change activity.
graph.experiment: Match fuels and verify local acid, recruitment and spontaneous EEG.

evidence: In a nicotine challenge, EEG discharges occurred in 6/7 control and 2/8 fenofibrate-fed mice. In an adult sleep-related epilepsy series, all 11 completers had a motor event in the follow-up overnight recording.
inference: Evoked protection, sleep movements and spontaneous seizures have different evidential value. Adult mouse total brain acid was 3.83 and 2.76 nmol/g at two sampling points.
hypothesis: A systemic response could improve fuel use. A local response could change nicotinic recruitment, while direct parent exposure can also depress mitochondrial respiration in a separate assay.
experiment: Measure native juvenile substrate use, then match glucose and ketones and verify local parent and acid, pathway engagement, initial recruitment and spontaneous activity.
limits: Adult whole-brain totals leave juvenile unbound exposure open. The pediatric lipid study does not establish WWOX efficacy or CNS exposure. Retain as a preclinical probe and defer pediatric priority.
